intent: Restore the 4 cm sensor row, which gave better progress in iteration 0, and keep the wider ±0.03 m spread with 15 mm spacing, which reduced s-bend line loss in iteration 1. Reduce yaw inertia by shortening the body to 0.14 m and lowering mass to 0.6 kg, so the robot responds faster to the same steering command on bends. Expect progress above 0.185 on the s-bend, line-loss events at or below 1 per run, and a score at or above 54.
learning: Hypotheses: (1) the row at y=0.04 with ±0.03 spread gives better progress than y=0.02, which implies the 4 cm lookahead helped on bends; (2) the wider spread reduces s-bend line loss below the baseline's 2 events; (3) lower yaw inertia from the shorter, lighter body reduces steering oscillation without costing progress. Ask the Integrator whether oscillation falls on the slalom compared with iteration 0 (0.163), whether the steering gain needed changed with the lighter body, and whether the robot now stalls or leaves the track on the s-bend. If progress drops while line loss stays low, the body change is the cause.
rationale: Iteration 1 scored 36.3, down from 54.3 in iteration 0. I changed two sensing factors at once (spread from ±0.02 to ±0.03 m and row from y=0.04 to y=0.02), so the drop cannot be assigned to one of them. The telemetry is clear on one point: the s-bend progress fell from 0.185 to 0.04. Line-loss events on the s-bend dropped from 2 to 1, so the wider spread did reduce line loss, but the robot still left the track. The shorter lookahead therefore did not pay off, and the 4 cm row gave better progress. Oscillation was roughly unchanged on the slalom (0.155 vs 0.163), so the y change did not clearly reduce jitter. max_error sits at 0.060 to 0.063 on every track in both iterations, which is the off-track floor. Body width cannot lift that floor because max(0.06, 0.0425 + body_width/4 ... ) stays at 0.06 across the allowed range, so the limit is fixed. The Integrator's note that kp was raised and kd lowered for signal scale is consistent with keeping 15 mm spacing and symmetric weights. Decision: keep the widened ±0.03 m spread (it lowered s-bend line loss) and restore the row to y=0.04, which gave the better progress. I also cut yaw inertia by shortening the body to 0.14 m and lowering mass to 0.6 kg, which reduces mass*(L²+W²)/12 from about 0.031 to about 0.017. A lower-inertia body should turn faster in response to the same wheel differential, which may let it hold the tape on bends. Wheel track and radius stay unchanged. Expected result: progress and line-loss events better than iteration 1, with a score at or above iteration 0. If it still falls below iteration 0, the body change is the suspect and I will revert it.
